newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 17.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.

- Prosecutors said they will summon four more politicians Rep. Seo Seok-jai of the ruling New Korea Party, former Home Affairs Minister Lee Dong-ho, Rep. Lee Seok-hyun of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics and former lawmaker Choi Doo-hwan.

- The Supreme Court will rule on the appeals of former presidents Chun Doo-hwan and Roh Tae-woo for their involvement in the Dec. 12 1979 military coup, the May 18, 1980 crackdown on the Kwangju uprising and the presidential slush fund scandal on Thursday.
- North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop will arrive in Seoul on Sunday from the Philippines, government officials said.
- A South Korean high-speed railway under construction which wil link Seoul and Pusan has structural problems on some of its bridges and may need to be partially rebuilt.
- President Kim Young-sam in a meeting with the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) General Secretary supported an early entry for China, Russia and Taiwan into the WTO.
- A private research insititute has revealed that Korea's unemployment rate hit 4.9 percent in real terms at the end of February, meaning more than 1 million people are out of work.
